correctness.rationale: The optimal pure Nash contributor count equals independent domination under the exact best-response model. The lower bound reconstructs a dominating set in G from one in H by adding at most one endpoint; upper bound replaces one of two selected endpoints by an independent dominating set of its private outside neighborhood and bounds these disjoint sets. Both endpoints are realized for all n>=4, the upper via four-path with balanced leaves for n>=6. Exhaustive exact standard-library checker confirms all 189587 labelled connected graph-edge additions for n=3..6 and checks both families to n=14. Finite tests corroborate, not replace, the analytic all-n arguments.

originality.rationale: An earlier related result already proves the same double-bouquet tree example, independent domination increase from 2 to k+1 and first positive order six. Neither that example nor the threshold is considered original here. The new theorem is a universal all-connected-graphs sharp two-sided bound i(G+e)-i(G) between -1 and floor((n-4)/2); no old claim or located literature theorem implies the universal inequality, lower cap and bound for every order. Statement/implication searches over best-shot, minimum maximal independent set, independent domination, edge addition, independent bondage/reinforcement and the exact formula found no covering result. The full economic paper, independence-domination and bondage survey texts, indexed vertex-stability paper and full edge-domination paper were materially inspected. Relevant unindexed equivalence risk persists.
residual_risks: Possible older or unindexed universal sharp edge-sensitivity theorems for independent domination; an already known double-bouquet witness and first positive graph size overlap with the present sharpness construction, so the theorem must be judged on the universal upper/lower bounds, not the witness. Direct publisher full-PDF access to some older sources was interrupted.

A standard order-half bound handles the tree-to-unicyclic (bipartite) witness class but not arbitrary connected final graphs; the general one-edge upper proof must not be conflated with that special-case bound.
Exact primary date is the archived 23 June 2009 public catalogue date; FEEM May 2009 month-only metadata exists, but day of any prior public release is not verified.

value.rationale: Optimizing pure equilibria in best-shot public-good networks is a motivated economic question. A previously known example already demonstrates a severe one-link deterioration; the new substantive contribution is the UNIVERSAL best-possible bound on how severe it can be at every network order together with an asymmetric proof that improvements can never exceed one. This answers a natural extremal network-design question, not just reproducing the existing counterexample. The exact universal bound has a structural private-neighbor replacement proof valid beyond trees and bipartite graphs.
